First, we find the eigenvalues of the matrix $A$ by solving $det(A-\lambda I)=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}|\begin{aligned}1-\lambda  & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -3-\lambda  & -1 \\ -5 & 4 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )|\begin{aligned}3-\lambda  & -1 \\ 4 & 2-\lambda \end{aligned}| & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )((-3-\lambda )(2-\lambda )+4) & =0 \\ (1-\lambda )({\lambda }^{2}+\lambda -2) & =0 \\ (\lambda -1)^{2}(\lambda +2) & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the eigenvalues are ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ (simple root) and ${\lambda }_{2}=1$ (double root).

Let's now find the dimension of the eigenspace corresponding to each eigenvalue.

- First, we consider the simple root ${\lambda }_{1}=-2.$ Since the root is simple, the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{-2}$ corresponding to ${\lambda }_{1}=-2$ is

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-2})=1.
$$

- Next, we consider the double root ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$ Let's find the dimension of the eigenspace ${V}_{1}$ corresponding to this eigenvalue. To do this, we row-reduce the matrix $A-1I:$

$$
\begin{aligned}A-1I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -3 & -1 \\ -5 & 4 & 2\end{aligned}]-1[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -4 & -1 \\ -5 & 4 & 1\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:={R}_{3}+{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}0 & 0 & 0 \\ 5 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}↔{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}5 & -4 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 0\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

In the reduced matrix above, there is one pivot column (the $1$st one). This implies that we will have $3-1=2$ linearly independent eigenvectors corresponding to ${\lambda }_{2}=1.$ So,

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{1})=2.
$$

Therefore, $A$ is diagonalizable, since

$$
\text{dim}({V}_{-2})+\text{dim}({V}_{1})=1+2=3.\,✓
$$

Finally, a corresponding diagonal matrix is 

$$
D=[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & -2\end{aligned}].
$$
